text:
sara.platform: quick note — after the v2 rate-tier change pushed at 09:15 UTC we're seeing a spike in 429s from iOS clients in eu-west. Support dashboard shows a cluster of errors starting ~09:18. Anyone on the rollout?

jess.support: saw the Alerts page. ~2.1k 429s in 12m for customers on plan 'starter-mobile'. Customers hitting /v1/generate (short payloads). Some opened tickets.

ryan.platform: that was my staged push — increased per-user per-min from 60 -> 120 for tier:starter to reduce throttling for web. Canary was set on 10% traffic, but looks like mobile traffic skewed the sample.

ryan.platform: config we rolled (snippet):
```yaml
rate_limits:
  starter:
    per_min: 120
    burst: 240
    scope: user
  pro:
    per_min: 1000
    burst: 2000
```

tony.sre: can you query the edge logs for 429 response headers? want to see which rule fired (rate_limit or quota_exceeded).

ops-bot: Alert: RateLimitSpike detected in eu-west on /v1/generate — 429 increase 6x over baseline (09:18-09:25).

jess.support: repro steps from a customer's device: curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -> 429 with x-rate-limit-retry-after: 37

ryan.platform: looking at api gateway logs — rule firing is rate_limit (per-minute window) not billing quota. The sample traffic rate distribution shows many starter users hitting bursts from background syncs. Canary % calc probably overweighted by a few high-frequency clients.

tony.sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) pause rollout (stop pushing new nodes into new policy) 2) revert to previous limits (per_min:60) 3) quick edge-side smoothing: increase burst window or add short retry-backoff header. Best is to pause+rollback to be safe.

jess.support: customers are getting upset. Recommend rollback and a short incident message + ETA for fix.

ryan.platform: agree. Initiating pause of further rollouts now. Running rollback plan B.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: rollback-rate-tier-starter -> target: eu-west. Command: `infractl rollout cancel --policy rate-tier-starter && infractl apply --file configs/rate-limits/v1/starter-rollback.yaml --region eu-west`

sara.platform: @ryan can you run the infractl commands? I'll coordinate support comms and draft a brief for customers.

ryan.platform: running commands now, pasting output:
```
$ infractl rollout cancel --policy rate-tier-starter
Cancelling staged rollout... done.
$ infractl apply --file configs/rate-limits/v1/starter-rollback.yaml --region eu-west
Applying config... success. Active config per_min=60 burst=120
```

tony.sre: confirming logs — 429 rate dropped back to baseline within 2 minutes of rollback. No evidence of quota-billing issues.

jess.support: messaging sent to affected customers: short note + apology + workaround (increase client-side jitter, exponential backoff).

sara.platform: follow-ups: (1) post-mortem to analyze canary weighting and traffic skewing, (2) add client-type segmentation to future canaries (mobile vs web), (3) consider edge smoothing knob before defaulting limits. I'll create the ticket.

ryan.platform: noted. I'll revert the rollout PR and add a canary filter by user-agent + traffic-weight floor.

tony.sre: add a monitoring alert for per-tier burst ratio and a synthetic mobile client test hitting /v1/generate to catch this earlier.

ops-bot: Incident closed: RateLimitTierRollback (eu-west) — root cause: canary sample skewed by high-frequency mobile clients.

sara.platform: thanks all. Closing this thread — please attach any trace IDs or raw logs to the post-mortem ticket. :thumbsup:
